land.text: Gaza Strip and the Jericho area, which Israel left under the Gaza-Jericho Agreement of 4 May 1994

predecessors.note: Israel held both from the 1967 war; the Gaza settlements and the Rafah crossing stayed with Israel (Gaza-Jericho page). The PLO, which signed, is not a Cliopatria state.

capitals.name: Ramallah
capitals.note: The page calls the PA 'Ramallah-based' and names no official capital or year; the Authority was 'formally inaugurated in Jericho on 5 July' 1994 (Gaza-Jericho page); the date of the move to Ramallah is not on the pages opened.

rulers.name: Yasser Arafat
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: 'Arafat became the PA's first president' on 5 July 1994 (Gaza-Jericho page); elected in the 1996 general election; died 11 November 2004 (PNA page).

rulers.name: Rawhi Fattouh
rulers.title: Acting president
rulers.note: From the death of Arafat, 11 November 2004.

rulers.name: Mahmoud Abbas
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: Won the presidency on 9 January 2005 with 62.3% of the vote; 'his term expired in 2009' (the page).

correction.text: the Gaza Strip and the Jericho area, the first land handed to the Authority

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks the PNA; its Israel row draws Gaza and the West Bank as one outline). 4 May 1994 Gaza-Jericho Agreement: 'Israel committed to partial withdrawals from Jericho and Gaza' within three weeks; the page gives no handover dates and says Israeli troops 'would remain at the Rafah border crossing and at Jewish settlements in the Gaza Strip'. The Jericho offer was 24 square miles (about 62 km2); the final area is not confirmed. The disc of 6 km is the researcher's; the PNA page says the PA nominally governed 60% of Gaza until August 2005, so the strip is drawn whole with that caveat.

correction.text: the Gaza Strip and the West Bank enclaves of Areas A and B

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Oslo II 'created the Areas A, B and C in the West Bank'; the PNA page gives A 18%, B 22%, C 60%, 'about 39%' administered by the PA. The eight 9 km discs (Jenin, Tulkarm, Qalqilya, Nablus, Ramallah, Bethlehem, Hebron, Jericho) come to about 2,000 km2 on the raster, 42% of the West Bank's 4,800 km2 of cells, to match the 39-40% (the pages name no towns: the researcher's reading). Area B's villages are not drawn. The 2002 reoccupation is a contest event; the 2000-2002 Intifada losses are undated on the pages.

correction.text: the whole Gaza Strip after the 2005 withdrawal, and the West Bank enclaves

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'The last soldier left the strip, and the Kissufim gate was closed on the early morning of September 12' 2005; the PNA page has the share of Gaza the PA governed nominally rise from 60% to 100%. Israel kept 'its borders, airspace, and sea (except the Egyptian border)'; the UN and ICJ still regard Gaza as occupied.

correction.text: the West Bank enclaves of Areas A and B only, after Hamas took Gaza on 14 June 2007

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'The PA became limited to the West Bank' after 14-15 June 2007; 'the PA currently administers about 39% of the West Bank, and 61% remains under Israeli control'; East Jerusalem 'was annexed by Israel in 1980'. Gaza is 'de jure under the PA, but governed by Hamas de facto since 2007' (the page) and is drawn under gaza-hamas.

region.text: the Gaza Strip and the Jericho area

ledger.note: 4 May 1994: the Authority is formed. The Gaza-Jericho Agreement was signed by Arafat and Rabin; 'the PA was formed on 4 May 1994' (PNA page). Israel was to withdraw from Jericho and part of Gaza within three weeks; Arafat returned to Gaza City on 1 July; the PA was 'formally inaugurated in Jericho on 5 July'. The pages give no handover date.

region.text: the West Bank towns of Areas A and B

ledger.note: 28 September 1995: Oslo II creates Areas A and B. 'The Accord was officially signed on 28 September 1995' in Washington by Rabin and Arafat; it 'created the Areas A, B and C in the West Bank'. The pages give neither the cities nor the dates of the redeployments; the eight town discs are the researcher's reading of 18% plus 22% of the West Bank.

region.text: Ramallah, Tulkarm, Qalqilya, Bethlehem, Jenin and Nablus

ledger.note: 29 March 2002: Operation Defensive Shield. The IDF reoccupied Ramallah on 29 March (Arafat's compound under siege), Tulkarm and Qalqilya on 1 April, Bethlehem on 2 April, Jenin and Nablus on 3 April. The Second Intifada page-wide: 'the PA lost control in some areas' without dates.

region.text: Ramallah, Tulkarm, Qalqilya, Bethlehem, Jenin and Nablus

ledger.note: May 2002: 'Israel withdrew from Palestinian cities in the West Bank' but 'maintained cordons of troops around certain towns and villages' and kept raiding; the infobox ends the operation on 10 May, the B'Tselem reference on 3 May. The pages do not say when each city returned to the PA.

12 September 2005: the Israeli withdrawal from Gaza is complete. Evacuations began on 15 August; 'the last soldier left the strip' on the early morning of 12 September; the IDF left the Philadelphi Corridor that day; no handover ceremony took place (the PA boycotted it). The share of the strip the PA governed nominally rose 'from 60% to 100%'.

14 June 2007: Hamas takes Gaza. 'Hamas took over Gaza on 14 June'; on 15 June Abbas dismissed the Hamas-led government and named Salam Fayyad prime minister; Hamas did not recognise it and 'the PA became limited to the West Bank'.

5 January 2013: 'State of Palestine'. Abbas 'ordered all embassies to replace references to the Palestinian Authority with State of Palestine'; the UN had voted to recognise Palestine as a non-member observer state in November 2012; the name has been used on official documents since January 2013. The territory does not change.

wars.name: Operation Defensive Shield

zones.text: Ramallah, Tulkarm, Qalqilya, Bethlehem, Jenin and Nablus

wars.outcome: 29 March 2002 Ramallah; 1 April Tulkarm and Qalqilya; 2 April Bethlehem; 3 April Jenin and Nablus; in May Israel withdrew from the cities but kept cordons and raids; the Second Intifada continued to 2005.
wars.note: The infobox gives 29 March to 10 May 2002, the B'Tselem reference 29 March to 3 May.

wars.name: Hamas takeover of Gaza
wars.outcome: 14 June 2007 Hamas took over Gaza; 15 June Abbas dismissed the Hamas-led government; the PA was left with the West Bank.
wars.note: The battle article was not opened (page budget); the dates are from the PNA page.

certainty.note: Areas A and B are enclaves cut by the Oslo II maps, but the pages opened give no towns or boundary lines, so city discs stand in for them; the Gaza line is the 1949 armistice line (not described on these pages). Exceptions: East Jerusalem (annexed by Israel in 1980, excluded from the Accords) and the Israeli-held parts of Gaza to September 2005.

sources.title: Palestinian National Authority
sources.note: Formation 4 May 1994, Areas A/B/C percentages (18/22/60), 2000-2002 losses, Abbas, the 2005 and 2007 changes, the January 2013 renaming and the 39% now administered. Page silent on a capital, on the Cairo and Taba agreements and on the Hebron Protocol.

sources.title: Gaza-Jericho Agreement
sources.note: Signed 4 May 1994 by Arafat and Rabin; Arafat to Gaza City 1 July 1994; PA inaugurated in Jericho 5 July 1994; the Jericho offer of 24 square miles. Page silent on handover dates.

sources.title: Oslo II Accord
sources.note: Signed officially 28 September 1995; created Areas A, B and C. Page silent on percentages, cities and redeployment dates.

sources.title: Israeli disengagement from Gaza
sources.note: Evacuation from 15 August 2005; completion 12 September 2005; four northern West Bank settlements evacuated 22 September 2005.

sources.title: Operation Defensive Shield
sources.note: Reoccupation of Ramallah (29 March 2002), Tulkarm and Qalqilya (1 April), Bethlehem (2 April), Jenin and Nablus (3 April); the May 2002 withdrawal with cordons.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks (the Cliopatria Israel and Palestinians rows do not draw the Authority's land). Written by me-10-x; 5 pages opened (budget up to 5). Not opened: the Cairo (1994) and Taba pages, the Hebron Protocol, the Wye River memorandum, the Battle of Gaza and the Areas A, B and C article (its title did not load). Disputes: the eight discs are the researcher's reading of Areas A and B; nothing in the pages opened lists the towns or their handover dates (the Oslo II page is silent on both), so the 1995 gain is dated by the signing. The pages differ on the end of Defensive Shield (3 or 10 May 2002). The four northern West Bank settlements evacuated on 22 September 2005 lie in Area C and are not a PA gain. The Gaza Strip is drawn whole from 1994 although Israel held about 40% of it with settlements until 2005 (the page gives 60% to 100%); the settlement blocs are not on any page. State of Palestine is not given its own dossier: the 2013 rename covers it, and it is also the Cliopatria-style name used by the gazetteer's country 'Palestine'. gaza-hamas (2007-06, written by another group) names this slug as predecessor, matching the 2007 loss. Ongoing: end year 2026 is the current year, no dissolve.
